A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FAST framework. The main text, seven tables, eleven figures, equations, and Appendices A.1–A.8 are available and can be matched across pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original segmentation experiments on MVTec-AD and BTAD, sampling and FARM ablations, and additional quantitative and qualitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains the original benchmark experiments, ablations, and appendix results. These remain original empirical outcomes even though most are unchanged.

M1.justification: AIAS, FARM, Algorithms 1–3, and the loss in A.3 retain the same procedures and components. The new related-work passage calls AIAS deterministic, but Algorithm 3 still samples Gaussian noise; this characterization does not document an actual algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same industrial anomaly synthesis and segmentation coverage on MVTec-AD and BTAD, including the appendix categories. The added mention of production-line changeover does not introduce an evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: The evaluated synthesis comparators remain CutPaste, DRAEM, GLASS, DFMGAN, RealNet, and AnomalyDiffusion. Sampling comparisons retain DDPM, DDIM, and PLMS. Newly discussed methods such as BDG are cited but not added to the experiments.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and A.5 retain the stated 500 samples per anomaly type, approximately one-third training allocation, mIoU/Acc metrics, segmentation backbones, and training and sampling settings. No new evaluation protocol accompanies the added discussion.

E4.justification: The sampler comparison, 2–1000-step sweep, FARM removal ablation, and qualitative examples in Section 4.3 and A.6–A.8 are retained. The new trade-off paragraph adds interpretation without an additional ablation, robustness test, or case study.

E5.justification: Both versions explicitly acknowledge the absence of classical error bars and retain the same checklist arguments about variability across categories and backbones. No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 1 corrects DFMGAN's average accuracy from 72.07 to 74.07, consistent with the unchanged category values averaging approximately 74.067. Other numerical results and displayed samples are retained. Section 4.3 also newly asserts that DDPM leads on visual-fidelity metrics, without reporting corresponding metric scores.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the temporal-smoothness condition from t in [te, ts] to t in [ts, te] while retaining ts > te, introducing a local inconsistency in the stated approximation domain. The closure lemmas, derivations, and proofs in A.1–A.2 otherwise remain unchanged apart from equation numbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: AIAS acceleration, FARM foreground reconstruction, and controllable synthesis supporting downstream segmentation. The central 10-step capability and reported FAST performance claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: A new Section 4.3 paragraph explicitly interprets AIAS's segmentation advantage as a trade-off between downstream utility and visual fidelity. v3 already discussed saturation and possible oversmoothing with excessive steps; v5 adds a more explicit distinction between evaluation objectives.

D1.justification: The pseudocode, prompt construction, hyperparameters, hardware and training information, and code-access disclosures remain the same, including A.4–A.5 and the checklist. No additional reproducibility information is supplied.

R1.justification: Section 2 gains a substantial foreground–background decoupling discussion covering PRN, DCDGANc, FCIS, and BDG, with an explicit originality argument distinguishing AIAS/FARM from BDG's inversion and attention mechanisms. Five cited works are added overall, substantially expanding positioning relative to closely related approaches.

P1.justification: v5 adds focused related-work and interpretation passages, makes scattered wording and terminology edits, updates the conference header and author contact text, and moves funding information into Acknowledgments. The overall section order and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: All figures and tables are retained, with unchanged figure graphics. Reflow relocates displays, including placing Figure 1 before the method overview and Figure 5 before Figure 6. Captions receive limited edits, including correcting Figure 8's appendix reference from A.6 to A.7.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly improves accuracy and context by correcting the DFMGAN average and expanding positioning against foreground–background methods. It supplies no new experimental validation. The benefit is tempered by the unsupported visual-fidelity ranking, the reversed time interval, and deterministic-sampler wording that conflicts with Algorithm 3's noise sampling; these issues limit the value of the added explanation.
